items.label: SPY5 + SPYL (S&P 500 duplication)
items.detail: SPY5 ($223,473.60, live get_account_positions) and SPYL ($119,857.92) both track the S&P 500 and together total $343,331.52 = 69.70% of NAV. Fresh 1-year daily-return correlation between the two (n=252, get_price_history closes Aug 2025-Aug 2026) is +0.9929 -- effectively one position split across two tickers.
items.recommendation: Trim SPYL (the smaller, more redundant leg, currently 6,240 shares) by roughly a third (~2,080 shares, ~$39,970 at $19.208) and redeploy into DBC (Invesco DB Commodity Index): this run's fresh correlation test found DBC to be the single best diversifier against both SPY5 (-0.1972) and SPYL (-0.2076) of seven candidates tested -- lower than SHY (-0.0382/-0.0443), which was the prior pick. Note DBC is itself a volatile, inflation-linked asset, not a low-vol ballast, so size it as a genuine diversifier, not a safety cushion (use the fixed-income ballast below for that).

items.label: Zero fixed-income ballast ahead of a live-repricing September FOMC
items.detail: get_pa_allocation (live) shows 0% of NAV in bonds -- 80.97% ETFs, 13.10% direct equities, 5.92% cash. CME FedWatch-derived odds of a 25bp September 16 hike stand near 60%, up from roughly 35% before Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Aug 28 Jackson Hole remarks (source: Reuters via CNBC, 'Jackson Hole analyst roundup,' Aug 31, 2026; CNBC 'September Fed decision is now a coin flip,' Aug 28, 2026).
items.recommendation: Establish a Treasury ballast sized at roughly 5% of NAV (~$24,500) in SHY (1-3Y): SHY showed the lowest correlation to the account's CRWV/GEV AI-infrastructure pair (-0.0573 of 7 candidates tested) and stayed in an extremely tight 81.35-83.20 range all year (2.2% total swing, confirming genuine duration ballast behavior), making it the most defensible shock absorber if the Fed surprises hawkish on Sept 16.

items.label: Available trading funds ($208.72) vs. reported cash balance ($28,311.97)
items.detail: get_account_summary (live) reports total_cash_value $28,311.97 (5.75% of NAV) but available_funds and buying_power of only $208.72; excess_liquidity is separately reported at $28,311.97 -- the same inconsistency in raw IBKR data flagged in this run's earlier passes today, still unresolved as of 18:15 UTC.
items.recommendation: Verify true buying power in the IBKR client before funding the DBC/SHY additions recommended here. If available funds are genuinely near-zero, fund them by trimming SPYL and the precious-metals cluster as sized above rather than deploying fresh cash.

items.label: Live position-value sum vs. reported net liquidation value
items.detail: Summing get_account_positions market values ($464,255.85) plus get_account_balances total_cash_value ($28,311.97) yields $492,567.82, which is $3,088.76 (0.63%) higher than get_account_summary's net_liquidation ($489,479.06) -- the latter figure is corroborated independently by get_pa_performance_all_periods' same-day 1D print of $489,491.48, so this run treats net_liquidation as the authoritative NAV and scales the bucket table below to it.
items.recommendation: No portfolio action needed -- this is a live-quote-vs-snapshot timing artifact (positions API appears to reflect a slightly fresher tick than the summary/balances snapshot). Worth a one-time check in the IBKR desktop client if it persists across future runs.

items.label: Precious-metals / mining cluster (IGLN, SSLV, KGC, NEM)
items.detail: IGLN ($41,294.48, 8.44%), SSLV ($7,771.48, 1.59%), KGC ($5,368.12, 1.10%) and NEM ($5,905.55, 1.21%) total $60,339.63 = 12.25% of NAV (get_account_positions, live). Gold traded near $4,380-4,410/oz in mid-to-late August 2026 -- still up sharply on the year but off January's all-time high -- with the Sept 10 CPI print and Sept 15-16 FOMC meeting flagged as the next decisive catalysts (sources: Yahoo Finance 'Gold prices today,' Aug 24, 2026; goldsilver.com 'Gold Price Outlook August 2026').
items.recommendation: Add TLT (iShares 20+ Year Treasury) as the cluster hedge: this run's fresh correlation test puts IGLN's 1-year correlation to TLT at +0.0506, the lowest of seven candidates tested (SHY +0.121, AGG +0.128, EFA +0.124, DBC +0.230, IEF +0.321, VWO +0.347) -- a shift from the IEF pick in earlier runs today, reflecting updated live data. Size at roughly 15-20% of the cluster's value (~$9,000-$12,000).

items.label: AI-infrastructure pair (CRWV, GEV) trades as one factor
items.detail: CRWV ($12,604.50, 2.57% of NAV, -$197.50 unrealized) and GEV ($8,920.20, 1.82% of NAV, -$828.70 unrealized) show a fresh 1-year daily-return correlation of +0.4291 (n=250, get_price_history closes) -- both remain geared to the same AI-datacenter capex cycle that drove NVIDIA's Aug 27 blowout Q2 print and the subsequent AI-trade rally.
items.recommendation: Trim CRWV specifically (the pair's higher-volatility leg, 58.6% of the pair's dollar value) by 30-50%, or lean on the SHY ballast above: a dollar-weighted CRWV/GEV blend (58.6%/41.4%) shows a -0.0573 correlation to SHY, the lowest of seven candidates tested this run (DBC -0.003, EFA +0.005, TLT +0.015, AGG +0.061, IEF +0.425, VWO +0.496).

items.detail: Account carries 0.94x leverage (gross_position_value $460,491.76 / net_liquidation $489,479.06) with $0 initial and $0 maintenance margin required (source: get_account_summary, live) -- no forced-selling risk from a margin call.
